decisions.reason: As an extension of the firm's established psychiatric and therapeutic offer with its own page, it is strategically well aligned and worth keeping while demand and reimbursement potential become clearer despite higher staffing costs.

The carpentry workshop fits the firm's sheltered-workshop and practical training capabilities, and although it is more market-exposed and costlier to run than a pure care service, it remains a reasonable option to retain for learning.

Outpatient sociotherapy is very close to the core service portfolio and relatively flexible to scale, so the firm is likely to keep this low-commitment option open even if website prominence is still limited.
A counseling service for senior living is highly consistent with the firm's eldercare expertise, low in fixed-cost risk, and its home-page visibility suggests strong strategic commitment.

The retail shop supports the sheltered-workshop model and social mission, but because consumer retail is more peripheral and uncertain for a care provider, it has the highest exit risk while still being worth keeping for now.
